key_idea: Inside a minimal invariant set, an idempotent from a compact semigroup of resolvent-built nonexpansive maps (Ellis–Numakura) gives an anchor point lying in the closed convex hull of its own limit points; a weighted tree of maps is built over it, and switching its leaves one at a time to an approximate fixed point produces unit vectors on which the Goebel–Karlovitz separating functionals along one branch stay at least 1/2, although those functionals must tend to zero on Y.
reason: The overall plan is striking and draws on deep sources: a minimal invariant set with the diameter lemma, an idempotent in a compact semigroup used as an anchor, and a telescoping leaf-switching argument that plays weak compactness off against functionals that vanish. But the core is a large inductive tree construction with budgets, tolerance schedules, ultrafilter limits, prediction sets and adaptive selection, so the reason the theorem holds is hard to see beneath the bookkeeping and the argument cannot be held in one's head.
recognized: no (claims to settle the open fixed point problem for nonexpansive maps on reflexive spaces; uses the Goebel–Karlovitz lemma and the Ellis–Numakura idempotent lemma)
